summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -2 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar −; brl −; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Class III milk +13.7%; weakest: Oats -14.4%. Key releases ahead: US Federal Funds Rate (10-28 2:00 PM ET); US FOMC Statement (10-28 2:00 PM ET); US FOMC Press Conference (10-28 2:30 PM ET); US Advance GDP q/q (10-29 8:30 AM ET); US Core PCE Price Index m/m (10-29 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.00% (-17 bp in a month), 2-year 4.68% (-13 bp); 2s10s curve +32 bp (-4 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.03% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 102.21 (+1.2% in a month, +4.0% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.388 (+3.8% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.656 (-0.8%); USD/MXN 18.62 (+5.0%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -0.9% in a month (+12.1% YTD); VIX 17.9. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 101.09 $/bbl (+14.0% in a month), Brent 110.01, ULSD 4.683 $/gal (+7.0%), natural gas 3.04 (-13.9%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -2.2% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.2%, Hang Seng -6.0%, yuan +0.8% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 12 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (36%); S&P GSCI +2.7% in a month; gold -6.8%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
